public_rationale: Zitron writes that "it appears" Microsoft is "being vague with its numbers to hide" that it is "spending hundreds of billions of dollars to buy GPUs that sit in warehouses or unpowered data centers, likely years in advance." The opening "it appears" and the word "likely" make this an inference, not a firm factual claim. Under the register's policy, a hedged inference is not scored. Part of the statement concerns Microsoft's reasons for its disclosures, and no evidence item addresses that. The packet has no source giving a dollar value for Microsoft GPUs that are uninstalled or unpowered. On November 2, 2025, Tom's Hardware reported that Satya Nadella said Microsoft did not have enough power to plug in some of the AI GPUs in its inventory (e1). That is context only. It gives no amount and was published in November 2025, before the September 2026 post.
limitations: The Nadella remark is from late 2025, gives no amount, and comes from a news report rather than a primary transcript.
No evidence item gives the value of Microsoft GPUs that are not installed or not powered as of September 2026.
No evidence item addresses why Microsoft describes its capacity the way it does.
"Hundreds of billions" may refer to total spending rather than to the value of idle GPUs.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Microsoft appears to be spending hundreds of billions on GPUs that sit in warehouses or unpowered data centers, likely bought years in advance, and is vague to hide this.

statement.excerpt: It appears that Microsoft is being vague with its numbers to hide the very obvious truth: that it’s spending hundreds of billions of dollars to buy GPUs that sit in warehouses or unpowered data centers, likely years in advance.

from_speaker: "Microsoft is being vague with its numbers to hide the very obvious truth"
"spending hundreds of billions of dollars to buy GPUs"
"that sit in warehouses or unpowered data centers"
our_interpretation: The sentence opens with "It appears that", and the timing part is hedged again with "likely". The speaker offers an inference, not a firm factual claim.
"Being vague ... to hide" is a claim about Microsoft's motive, which cannot be checked.
Microsoft does not disclose the value of GPUs bought but not installed or powered, so the size claim ("hundreds of billions") rests on the speaker's estimates.
Under the register's policy, a hedged inference is not scored. It is recorded as not adjudicable.
criteria.support_condition: Not scored. It could only be supported if a primary source showed Microsoft held GPUs worth hundreds of billions of dollars that were uninstalled or unpowered, and that it withheld this on purpose.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Not scored. It could only be contradicted if a primary source showed Microsoft's uninstalled or unpowered GPU stock was far below hundreds of billions of dollars.
